newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean workers clash with riot police in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean workers clash with riot police in Seoul.

text.p: Thousands of South Korean workers clashed with riot police on Thursday after Labour Day ceremonies in Seoul, witnesses said.
Riot police used teargas to stop members of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions from marching in central Seoul, witnesses said.

About 7,000 workers joined by some students attended ceremonies at a park where they denounced President Kim Young-sam's administration and demanded that Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, be arrested.
Witnesses said protesters threw Molotov cocktails, but it was unclear whether they were thrown by students or workers.
About 15 people, mostly workers, were detained and one man who was beaten by police was taken to hospital, witnesses said. His condition was not immediately known.
The junior Kim has been embroiled in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal surrounding the collapse of Hanbo Steel, and two of his close associates were arrested on Wednesday.
The local press has reported that Hyun-chul will soon be arrested on allegations that he received bribes from businesses.
The confederation, which has 500,000 members, spearheaded almost a month of work stoppages in January following the passage of a labour law that was rammed through parliament on December 26.
The law weakened job stability by allowing employers to lay off workers and hire temporary workers from outside the company during a strike.
The January strikes ended with a promise from the government to revise the law. A revised bill was passed in March, postponing layoffs for two years.
